doc.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012

title: Heavy metal guitarist at 16 gets a call to play big band piano
summary: Weber was a heavy metal guitarist playing bars at 16 when Mark Kleckley called him to join a Sunday big band; he had started piano at three.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: As you can tell there’s a lot of stuff going on.
It’s a pleasure to be here. Actually I understand there’s a parade, there’s bagpipes, there’s a ton of people, and it’s the Bicentennial. How many colleges can say that in America?
Really. But I’ve been practicing this little bit, because I can use this intro with you and no one else. Jon Weber, heavy metal guitarist, whose life was changed by a big band.

Yes. You have done your reading. Yes that’s exactly — I was a heavy metal guitarist. I was 16 playing with guys older than me in bars, playing heavy metal. God knows where I would have been had I pursued that path — I may be deaf or dead, or who knows what. But I happened to get a phone call from a guy named Mark Kleckley. This was in Milwaukee where I grew up. I was 16. And he said, “Our big band piano player just quit. We have a big band that rehearses every Sunday and we need somebody. I heard you’re a pretty good jazz piano player.” “Well I’m a guitar player now, I haven’t touched a piano in two years.”
Okay. And then you went to the guitar.

Yes, I mean, again, every kid has this struggle of do I play baseball, do I play a musical instrument and get beaten up for playing tuba or accordion or whatever instrument. Even piano wasn’t as cool as guitar. For some reason I thought I have to be a guitar player. Which, it helped. I sort of learned how to have some dexterity in my left hand. I paid attention to it more than I would have otherwise I suppose. But heavy metal guitar, that was where I was, and thank God Mark Kleckley, what a great name and what a great person/mentor in my life he turned out to be.
